prompt_variants: Test the unreleased Nutshell change at https://github.com/cashubtc/nutshell/pull/1095. Build its exact PR head, then use that candidate as the mint in a disposable regtest lab with Bitcoin Core, LND 0.21, and a compatible Nutshell wallet. Bring the lab online, fund the wallet with 2048 sat through the normal mint flow, report its balance, export compact evidence with the PR commit and image digest, and fully tear down the lab. Use only Proofstorm.

Using only Proofstorm, try https://github.com/cashubtc/nutshell/pull/1095/ as a real mint. Let the candidate build continue through bounded waits, use its exact catalog version with Bitcoin Core, LND 0.21, and a compatible wallet, and complete a normal 3072 sat wallet funding flow. Report the result, preserve commit and image provenance in compact evidence, and remove the disposable lab.

Validate Nutshell PR https://github.com/cashubtc/nutshell/pull/1095 end to end. Build the frozen PR revision, select the resulting candidate mint version, and run it in the smallest useful Bitcoin Core plus LND 0.20 regtest lab with a compatible wallet. Fund 4096 sat into the wallet, report the observed balance, export evidence identifying the commit and image, then verify teardown. No operator commands.

Can the Nutshell code in https://github.com/cashubtc/nutshell/pull/1095/ actually run? Have Proofstorm build it and recover through repeated waits if necessary. Put the exact candidate mint in a disposable Bitcoin Core and LND 0.21 lab with a compatible wallet, complete a 1536 sat mint-funded wallet flow, capture compact provenance and runtime evidence, and clean everything up.

Build a disposable system that tests Nutshell Lightning payments at different routing fee rates. Use two Nutshell mints, one backed by LND and one by CLN, connected through a Lightning network. Test payments in both directions with routing fees below and above the mint's fee reserve. Report quote states, reserved and paid fees, balances, and whether value was conserved. Export evidence and fully tear down the lab.

Create an isolated regtest experiment with a Nutshell mint on LND and another on CLN. Route payments through an intermediate Lightning node in both directions. Compare a cheap route with a route whose fee exceeds the melt reserve, and show the observed quote states, fee reserve, actual fee, wallet balances, and conservation result. Preserve evidence, then remove everything you created.

Test 2,000 sat cross-mint payments between LND-backed and CLN-backed Nutshell mints. Exercise both directions first with about a 1 sat routing fee and then with about a 100 sat routing fee, keeping the mints' normal reserve behavior. Report the exact settlement and accounting observations, export evidence, and verify complete teardown.

Build a disposable regtest lab with one Bitcoin node and two directly connected LND nodes. Fund a channel, prove a Lightning payment can cross it, capture useful evidence, and fully tear down the lab.

Create the smallest useful CLN-to-CLN regtest network backed by Bitcoin Core. Open a funded channel, exercise connectivity and a payment-capable path, report what happened, export evidence, and verify that teardown removed the lab.

Build an isolated CDK mint lab that uses its supported embedded LDK Lightning backend rather than an external payment-backend node. Add a compatible wallet, prove a basic mint and payment workflow, explain the resolved dependencies, export evidence, and tear everything down.

Exercise a CDK mint with an embedded LDK backend on regtest using a compatible wallet. Do not invent an external payment_backend link when the catalog says the backend is embedded. Record balances and settlement evidence and finish with verified teardown.

Spin up a disposable regtest CDK-LDK mint and a wallet that works with it. Put 15,000 sats into the wallet through Lightning, demonstrate one payment, save enough evidence to support the result, and remove the lab when finished.

Create a disposable Lightning regtest lab, establish a working route, partition the route, demonstrate the expected loss of reachability, heal it, and demonstrate recovery. Export the ordered evidence and fully tear down the lab.

Build a small Bitcoin-backed Lightning network and test a node restart: establish healthy connectivity, restart one routing node, observe the interruption and recovery, preserve evidence, and verify complete teardown.

Build a disposable lab for a supported mint and wallet authentication flow. Exercise an authenticated spend and a replay attempt, report which actions were accepted or rejected with evidence, and fully tear down the lab.

Use Proofstorm to test replay protection for an authenticated mint operation in an isolated lab. Include the necessary identity dependency, capture conformance and replay observations, export evidence, and verify teardown.

Build a disposable Bitcoin, LND, Nutshell mint, and wallet lab. Use each component's native CLI in its real running container to show Bitcoin and Lightning are healthy. Restart the mint, verify it returns without losing its persistent state, export evidence, and tear the lab down.

Create a small regtest system using Bitcoin Core, CLN, a Nutshell mint, and a wallet. Prove bitcoin-cli and lightning-cli can talk to the actual running services, restart the wallet and mint, and show both recover. Keep offline inspection separate from commands that need a live process. Save evidence and remove the lab.

Make a disposable CDK-on-LND lab with a compatible wallet. Exercise a normal wallet flow, inspect one implementation detail offline, then run a native status command in the live LND container and restart the mint. Verify the lab still works, export evidence, and clean up.

Build a disposable cross-mint Nutshell payment lab and create an unroutable Lightning payment so the payer wallet has a failed or pending melt. Poll that exact payer-side melt quote through the wallet, show whether its reserved proofs are released, restart the payer mint and verify recovery, export evidence, and tear everything down. Prove that the intended route is actually interrupted, including established connections. A reservation-release result requires nonzero reserved proofs immediately before refresh, zero afterward, the expected restored available balance, and a subsequent successful spend. If the failure leaves no reservation, report that attempt as inconclusive for release; do not fabricate wallet state.

Create a small regtest system with two independently backed mints and one wallet per mint, establish a funded cross-mint baseline, then break the Lightning route and attempt a payment. Reconcile the exact payer-side melt quote using the wallet's typed refresh operation and report before-and-after state, reserved proof count, and spendable balance. Restart the payer mint, preserve evidence, and fully clean up. Prove that the intended route is actually interrupted, including established connections. A reservation-release result requires nonzero reserved proofs immediately before refresh, zero afterward, the expected restored available balance, and a subsequent successful spend. If the failure leaves no reservation, report that attempt as inconclusive for release; do not fabricate wallet state.

Plan a lab containing a mint that requires an unsupported payment backend and a channel whose requested outbound liquidity exceeds its funding. Do not materialize an invalid lab. Report the exact feasibility failures and compatible alternatives.

Ask Proofstorm to plan an impossible mixed implementation topology with incompatible wallet and mint versions. It must fail before materialization, explain the dependency mismatch, and suggest valid catalog alternatives without creating infrastructure.

Build a disposable Bitcoin Core, LND, Nutshell mint and Nutshell wallet regtest lab. Prefer the software's native CLIs for operating and inspecting components; use Proofstorm for provisioning, coordination, lifecycle and evidence. Discover CLI help and demonstrate substantive native Bitcoin and Lightning health queries. Make a small reversible native mutation, then verify its effect through a Proofstorm typed observation and explain any visibility limitation. Discover and use the wallet CLI to report its mint configuration and balance. Inspect one implementation detail offline, restart a component and verify recovery in its real running environment. Explain which typed operations earned their use. Preserve ordered evidence and fully tear down. Use only Proofstorm access to the lab; no operator or host commands.

Using Proofstorm, test candidate input rejection for https://github.com/cashubtc/nutshell/pull/not-a-number and https://github.com/example/unsupported-proofstorm-repository/pull/1, requesting implementation nutshell. Submit each to candidate validation without creating a lab. Report the distinct refusals, whether any build was admitted, and the supported recovery path. Do not substitute another PR or build a valid candidate. No operator commands.

Design a disposable regtest experiment to distinguish routing-fee refusal from insufficient directional liquidity and loss of connectivity. Use at least three Lightning nodes so the measured payment crosses an intermediate hop, with independently backed payer and receiving endpoints. Establish a successful baseline, exercise asymmetric liquidity and changed routing fees, and explain which condition caused each observed outcome. Prefer native CLIs to inspect and operate software, discovering help as needed. Use Proofstorm for provisioning, coordination, faults, lifecycle and evidence. Record routes, actual fees, balances and accounting boundaries. Do not infer a refusal cause from a generic error alone. Export evidence and fully tear down; no operator commands.

Design a disposable network experiment with two independently testable paths and an unaffected control. Establish baseline service access through native component CLIs. Apply overlapping network partitions and verify they interrupt the intended traffic, including established connections. Heal only one fault and show that the other remains effective, then restore all paths. Prefer native CLIs for observations and operations, using Proofstorm for topology, faults, lifecycle and evidence. Explain any difference between transport reachability and service recovery. Preserve ordered evidence and fully tear down; no operator commands.

Design a disposable regtest payment network to determine what happens to in-flight work when a payment component restarts. Establish a successful native CLI payment baseline, run a bounded sequence of payments, and restart a component while work is active. Use native CLIs for software operation and Proofstorm for coordination, lifecycle and evidence. Demonstrate actual temporal overlap, correlate each attempted payment with its final outcome, account for funds and fees, and prove a subsequent payment works. If overlap or finality cannot be established, report that limitation explicitly. Bound and stop all traffic before exporting evidence and fully tearing down; no operator commands.

Design a disposable regtest network to find the boundary at which directional Lightning liquidity prevents further payments and whether service recovers when liquidity is restored. Use a successful baseline and a bounded native CLI payment workload, observe exhaustion without assuming a generic payment error proves its cause, then restore liquidity and demonstrate a successful payment. Prefer native CLIs for operations and measurements; use Proofstorm for provisioning, coordination, lifecycle and evidence. Account for balances, fees and unresolved work before and after recovery. Preserve evidence and fully tear down; no operator commands.

Use Proofstorm to design and provision a disposable regtest network with Bitcoin Core and two LND nodes. Operate the software through its native CLIs: discover the commands, fund and confirm a channel, create an invoice and pay it across that channel. Prove the route and settlement from native observations, account for the payment and fees, then preserve ordered evidence and fully tear down. Use Proofstorm for lab lifecycle, execution and evidence. No host or operator commands.

Build a disposable regtest lab with two independently backed Nutshell mints and one wallet per mint. Establish a funded cross-mint payment baseline. First live-check the corrected melt-refresh receipt: refresh an existing exact quote and independently compare the receipt's total available wallet balance with native read-only wallet state and a balance observation, accounting for reserved=NULL as unreserved. If they disagree, preserve the discrepancy and do not claim the receipt validated. Then exercise genuine wallet-crash recovery: interrupt the Lightning route and prove established connectivity is actually gone; start a real payer wallet payment using its native CLI, observe actual nonzero reserved proofs in its database using read-only inspection, and terminate that CLI process while its reservation still exists. Native process supervision and bounded polling are allowed. Do not edit wallet tables, fabricate reservations, modify wallet code, or simulate a payment with a stub. Preserve ordered timestamps, the exact melt quote, native command results and the real reservation immediately before and after process termination. Reconcile that exact quote with Proofstorm's wallet_melt_quote_refresh. A release pass needs an authoritative UNPAID quote, nonzero reserved count and amount immediately before refresh, zero after, and the corresponding increase in available balance independently verified with native state. If the timing misses the reservation or the quote remains PAID/PENDING, retain the attempt as inconclusive and adapt within a bounded attempt budget; do not substitute an ordinary failed payment as proof of release. Heal the route, prove restored spendability with a successful payment, restart the payer mint and wallet, and prove another successful payment after restart with balances and fees reconciled. Stop all supervised/background processes, export evidence, and tear down. Use native CLIs for the interrupted payment and process control; existing typed setup/observation operations are available where justified. Distinguish network-fault effects from the explicit wallet crash and distinguish observed facts from inferred failure mechanisms.

Determine whether a new agent can discover and operate the installed CDK CLI wallet using Proofstorm. Build exactly one disposable regtest lab with a CDK 0.18.0 mint configured with input_fee_ppk=0, two CDK CLI 0.18.0 wallet components, Bitcoin Core and sufficient LND infrastructure for real Lightning funding and payment. Discover exact catalog/configuration and native CLI help. Use native wallet operations to initialize, fund one wallet with a small BOLT11 payment and pay a separate Lightning invoice. Compare the passive Proofstorm wallet_balance observation with independent native evidence, and verify the second wallet stays empty and has separate state. CDK native commands can recover incomplete operations, even balance; distinguish those calls from passive observations. Restart the funded wallet, verify identity and balance persistence, and complete a further small payment. Use explicit bounded command supervision for potentially blocking native processes, retain actual exit codes, and verify cleanup of child processes. Do not replay an ambiguous payment or fabricate/edit proofs. Keep seed/proof material and payment preimages out of outputs; small BOLT11 requests may be used through the authorized native surface, while ecash token transfer is outside this checkpoint. Explain any discovery friction or unsupported typed operation. Use only Proofstorm access, no host/operator commands. Export evidence and fully tear down. Reserve the final 20 percent of the run for evidence and cleanup; stop after two equivalent failures without a changed hypothesis. This is a discovery and interoperability smoke test, not a crash-recovery test.

Planning-only diagnostic: use Proofstorm catalog discovery and lab_plan to prepare a regtest topology containing Bitcoin Core, two LND nodes, one CDK 0.18.0 mint, and two CDK CLI 0.18.0 wallets. Bind both LND nodes to Bitcoin, the mint to one LND node, and the LND nodes as Lightning peers. The mint must explicitly use input_fee_ppk=0 in its authored config. Do not apply or materialize any plan, build images, create experiments, or run runtime actions. Read the resulting receipt and verify that the zero-fee override is present, rather than merely stating it is present. If it is absent, submit an actually corrected request with new plan and idempotency IDs; stop after two equivalent requests. Report the final plan ID, digest and exact mint configuration, or the specific blocker. All evidence for this diagnostic is the planning transcript and stored draft; no experiment export or lab teardown is needed. Use only Proofstorm tools.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: Prefer direct argv with default private output for CDK funding/claim/payment commands. Native exit and cleanup receipts plus independent recipient settlement and passive wallet balances establish the outcome; you do not need to parse CDK text to complete this zero-fee smoke. Use json_fields for native JSON, especially LND sendpayment and recipient lookup. Public output is restricted to safe help, hashes and explicitly extracted setup/BOLT11/payment-hash values. Never publish raw payment output or grep-selected/redacted payment lines. If a native text receipt is actually needed, keep the raw file private and project strictly parsed enumerated/numeric fields; an unknown format is a parsing error, never a fabricated FAILED status or zero amount.

Operate CDK CLI wallets on the operator-verified plan supplied below. This is an assisted-setup wallet smoke test, not a lab-design test. Do not create, edit or replace plans; apply the supplied exact plan digest to one disposable instance. Component roles: btc is Bitcoin Core 30.0; lnd-a is the CDK mint backend; lnd-b is the independent Lightning funding payer and invoice recipient; mint is CDK 0.18.0 with explicit input_fee_ppk=0; wallet-1 and wallet-2 are CDK CLI 0.18.0 with separate persistent /wallet volumes. Before executing node commands, read the catalog native invocation hints for Bitcoin Core, LND and CDK CLI; do not guess credential paths or assume jq/curl are installed. Read native subcommand help before wallet mutations. Provisioning readiness does not mean payment readiness: establish a direct channel and independently verify at least 100000 sat of usable outbound liquidity in EACH direction, above channel reserves and commitment fees, before starting wallet funding. Both directions are needed even though the wallet initially receives only 5000 sat. Discover and perform this setup through native CLIs; use a push amount or a separate node-to-node rebalance without increasing the wallet funding amount. Initialize both wallets natively, record only hashes of their seed identities, and confirm independent state with wallet-2 empty. Fund wallet-1 with 5000 sat through a real Lightning payment from lnd-b, explicitly finish mint issuance, and compare native evidence with passive wallet_balance for mint. Pay a separate 700-sat lnd-b invoice natively, verify recipient settlement and fees without printing preimages, and check 4300 sat remains with zero reserved/pending amounts. Restart wallet-1, check its identity and balance persisted, pay another 300-sat lnd-b invoice, independently verify settlement and final balance 4000 sat; wallet-2 must remain empty. Use cdk-cli --work-dir /wallet/cdk --unit sat --non-interactive on every invocation. Native balance can recover sagas, so distinguish it from the passive observation. In this pinned release mint-pending checks pending proofs, not paid quote issuance: resume the exact existing paid quote with mint <url> --quote-id <id>. Use a short explicit --wait-duration when creating an unpaid quote, or extract its invoice from a component-local file while the supervised handle remains live; do not block waiting for funding that has not been sent. Use the shared component_exec_live supervisor: argv for direct command scope or script for shell scope, an explicit execution timeout of at most 300 seconds, operation_wait for receipts, and action_cancel for owned operations. Never use nohup or background jobs. Inspect exit_code, exit_signal, timed_out and cleanup_verified, not just operation phase. Shell wrappers must capture the native command exit status immediately and exit with that status after safe output parsing; do not replace it with the parser or a later balance command exit status. Keep CDK payment text private; use a parsed receipt only when independent observations cannot answer the question. Never retry ambiguous payments without checking their outcomes. LND native data is at /home/lnd/.lnd. Execution output is private by default. For LND sendpayment use --force --json and output mode json_fields selecting status and failure_reason; do not print its raw output or attempt generic redaction. Use json_fields for other supported safe receipt fields. CDK table/text output may remain entirely private. Do not write a parser just to reproduce evidence already available from settlement and passive balances. Public output is allowed for safe help, seed fingerprints and explicitly extracted BOLT11/payment-hash/setup values; never expose seed, proof or preimage values. Command requests are journaled: keep sensitive inputs in component-local files. Small BOLT11 requests may pass through the authorized surface; ecash token transfers are outside scope. Use only Proofstorm tools, no host commands. Keep retries bounded: after two equivalent failures without a changed hypothesis, report the blocker and clean up. Reserve the final 20 percent for process cleanup, evidence export and verified lab teardown. Report which milestones were actually reached, distinguish discovery friction from wallet defects and harness failures, and do not claim recovery safety from a normal restart. Keep the report concise and finish it before the hard cap. Native payments are not counted as typed paid_melts; use recipient settlement and wallet balances as evidence.

Work economically: use catalog_entry_read once per relevant kind, bounded waits for handles, and batch independent observations. Avoid repeated full help or receipt dumps. wallet_balance takes the mint component ID mint, whereas cdk-cli takes its URL. Finish with a concise evidence-backed report; treat an unmet output-policy condition as a failed gate, even when money movement succeeds.

Exercise the shared native execution contract on the operator-verified small plan supplied below. This is an execution-reliability test with assisted setup, NOT a wallet funding or recovery test. Apply the supplied plan directly; do not create or edit plans. Roles: chain is Bitcoin Core 30.0, lightning is LND 0.20.0-beta, wallet is CDK CLI 0.18.0. Do not fund wallets, mine, open channels, make payments, restart the controller or replace pods. Use only authorized Proofstorm tools.
Create an experiment and acquire a lease covering the bounded run. Use unique operation IDs for distinct cases. Discover the current component_exec_live schema. Provide exactly one command form: argv for command exit scope, or script for shell exit scope. Submit and retain operation handles; wait for native receipts rather than inferring success from operation phase. Use public output only for safe native CLI help/version on both lightning and wallet. Keep other output private by default. Do not launch nohup jobs, install utilities or invent wallet-specific wrappers.
Generate a fresh synthetic secret canary inside wallet and store a small JSON document locally with that canary in payment_preimage plus known safe fields status=SUCCEEDED and value_sat=7. Never put the canary value in requests, public output, projections or reports; no real seed/proof material is needed. Exercise reading that file once with default private output and once with json_fields selecting status and value_sat. Require empty ordinary stdout/stderr and inspect capture byte/hash metadata; selected output must contain only the requested safe fields. Do not read private capture files back into public output or reconstruct the canary outside the component. Explain the limits of what you verified.
Exercise a known nonzero command exit (for example argv invoking /bin/sh -c 'exit 7') and a separate script exit to distinguish command versus shell exit_scope. Exercise malformed/table output with json_fields and a known nonzero exit: require a static projection failure with no raw-output fallback while preserving the command exit status. Inspect truncation/completeness flags; do not turn an expected nonzero exit into a failure claim about the supervisor.
Start one long supervised operation with a component-local start marker. Confirm it genuinely began through a separate bounded marker check, then request action_cancel and wait for its native cancelled/cleanup receipt. Separately let a started operation reach its own short execution deadline and retain timed_out, exit/signal and cleanup evidence. A wait-tool timeout is not this deadline. Require cleanup_verified=true on terminal cases; retain unknown/unverified outcomes honestly and close the lab rather than replay an uncertain mutation. Do not infer actual descendant absence beyond the supervisor receipt or claim controller-restart coverage.
After these cases, deliberately observe the runner's cleanup admission boundary. Use at most two harmless, owned supervisor timer operations if a time witness is needed; each execution deadline is at most 300 seconds. Plan their timing from receipt timestamps and the run budget so a live handle spans the boundary; use bounded status/wait calls, preferably at most 45 seconds. Do not pad model steps with redundant discovery or repeatedly launch experimental commands. If cleanup activates early, preserve partial results and proceed directly to cleanup.
At or after the boundary, make exactly one new harmless exec request intended as the admission probe, using a new operation ID; expect cleanup_phase_only before MCP. A pre-boundary success is not a refusal result. Cancel/wait for any remaining owned operations, release the lease, close the experiment, export evidence, close the lab, verify absence, and produce a concise final report before the hard cap. Public help is the only intended public output. Report exact operation IDs and observed receipt fields, separate expected refusals from defects and discovery friction, and distinguish a passed target property from a clean agent completion. Do not launch additional scenarios.

Run one unfunded cocod lifecycle checkpoint on the supplied exact operator-verified plan. Planning and the documented API contract are assisted; do not replan. Operate wallet-1 only. Select cocod-wallet 0.0.17-dev.44e5101c, source 44e5101cbea370132af6e68f88e01b47e39431c4, image sha256:88dc907f64530788280b0ba603b1bd7f361c58281171e74ca25b0676fadfcdc7. No funding, wallet-2 initialization, channels, ecash exchange, second daemon, daemon kill or controller faults.

Read the wallet catalog once. Limit discovery to cocod wallet initialize --help and cocod session start --help, plus at most one optional bounded read of immutable upstream documentation/source. Such public reads are explicitly allowed: /opt/coco/packages/cocod/docs/API.md or src/v1/schema.ts under that same package. This permission never covers live wallet files, credentials, configuration or recovery responses. Do not scan source broadly or infer routes/methods from documentation.

Use direct argv ["cocod","health"] with output {"mode":"json_fields","fields":["status"]}. Use direct argv ["cocod","status"] with output {"mode":"json_fields","fields":["seedAccess.state","seedAccess.requiresPassphrase","cocoSession.state"]}. The shared projection validates finite enums/booleans; native seedAccess:null yields null selected leaves. Never use public raw health/status or custom status filters. Retain projection success and actual native exit/signal, timeout, cleanup, completeness and truncation receipts.

Native clients inherit COCOD_URL=http://127.0.0.1:62626 and must not autostart another daemon. Keep every mutation private. Where file inputs require a shell, invoke the native command alone/with exec so its exit is preserved; observations get separate operations. Generate a private component-local passphrase file with mode 0600, then independently observe its numeric mode. Never embed passphrase or credential values in journaled requests.

Exact documented identity API: POST http://127.0.0.1:62626/v1/admin/wallet/recovery-material, Authorization: Bearer read privately from /wallet/.cocod/credentials/current/client, JSON body {"passphrase": value read privately from your passphrase file}. The response is {"mnemonic": string}. Inside the component, validate that exact top-level field as a nonempty string and publish only its SHA-256. Never print the response or heuristically extract words from CLI text. Do not enumerate paths/methods or call unrelated administrative endpoints. No recovery API discovery is required.

Complete these observations in order, batching independent reads:
